newsitem.title: INDIA: Forty feared dead as fire hits packed Delhi cinema.
newsitem.headline: Forty feared dead as fire hits packed Delhi cinema.

text.p: About 40 people were feared dead and 60 were injured on Friday when fire ripped through a packed cinema hall in the Indian capital, rescue officials said.
Dozens of fire tenders and rescuers worked feverishly to pull people trapped by smoke in the cinema in a Delhi suburb.
Delhi's deputy chief fire officer R.C. Sharma told Reuters about 40 people were thought to have died in the blaze and another 60 had been taken to nearby hospitals.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the cinema hall, which was full for a matinee screening of a popular Hindi movie, can seat 1,400 people.
Karan Samir, who escaped from the cinema minutes after the fire broke out, said: "It started 15 minutes after the intermission. There were a lot of people inside."
There was pandemonium in the narrow streets near the cinema as spectators jostled firemen and police officials trying to tend to the victims as they were brought out on stretchers.
Fireman Hiralal More said when he went into the cinema at least 30 people were trapped inside. "I must have saved at least ten women and three children."
U.S. Chillar, a fire official at the scene said more than 60 people were taken to hospital.
He said the fire started when an electrical transformer on the ground floor exploded and set fire to cars in an adjacent parking lot.
"When I went up most of the people were huddled in two bathrooms," Chillar said.
